stem: Two plants have similar height, but one has much denser lateral branching and poorer lower-canopy light. What does this demonstrate?
choices: Plant height alone is not a complete canopy-architecture metric
The taller plant is always more uniform
Lower-canopy light is unrelated to architecture
One top-canopy PPFD reading describes the whole plant
rationale: Architecture includes branch distribution and canopy porosity; similar height can produce very different internal light environments.
